title: Home / Overview with app shell
brief: Redesign of the Engram Explorer home screen and app shell for a professional, eye-catching local-first dashboard that shows an AI agent's long-term memory (Engram) and the user's AI coding sessions across vendors (Claude Code, Codex). Dark theme by default, light supported. All directions use only the synced tokens in design/system.md; the chart and project-lobe series colors are a proposed palette (--series-1..8), not yet tokenized, and are labelled as such inside each artboard. Brain first (02) is the chosen visual base; 04-06 are scroll-behaviour variants built on top of it.

artboards.title: Command center
artboards.tradeoff: Dense 12-column bento grid: every number above the fold and fast to scan; more to take in at first glance and the brain is one tile among others

artboards.title: Brain first
artboards.tradeoff: Full-bleed knowledge-graph hero with glass KPI cards and a 64px icon rail: strongest first impression and brand; less data above the fold and heavier rendering

artboards.title: Editorial timeline
artboards.tradeoff: Calm typographic layout around one unified timeline of memories and agent sessions: elegant and very readable; slower to spot operational problems and less spectacle

artboards.title: Scroll A: collapsing hero
artboards.tradeoff: Hero stays sticky and shrinks into a 72px bar with the search docked and a pinned KPI strip: title, search and KPIs always at hand; the graph becomes decorative once collapsed and KPI captions and links are hidden until you scroll back up

artboards.title: Scroll B: parallax depth + staggered reveal
artboards.tradeoff: Hero moves at 0.4x with depth-layered nodes and sections reveal on entry: strongest sense of depth and a lively first scroll; more scroll code to keep correct and the hero is lost once scrolled past

artboards.title: Scroll C: zoom into memory + synapse thread
artboards.tradeoff: Camera zooms into the most active project while the hero fades, and a synapse thread grows down the left gutter lighting one node per section: the most narrative and distinctive; heaviest to render and the hero controls fade away after 420px
